easy.def: The place where an animal or plant lives.
examples: A pond is a frog's habitat.
The sea is a whale's habitat.
A bird's habitat can be a forest.

more.def: The natural home of a plant or animal, where it finds what it needs to live.
examples: The desert is the habitat of many lizards and snakes.
When forests are cut down, animals lose their habitat.
The zoo built a habitat that looks like a snowy mountain.

easy.def: The soft threads that grow on your head.
examples: She has long hair.
Brush your hair.
My dog's hair is soft.

more.def: The thin threads that grow on the head and body of a person or animal.
examples: She tied her long hair back with a ribbon.
A hair from the cat's tail was stuck to my sweater.
Most mammals have hair or fur on their bodies.
I ate half of the apple.
Half of the class is here.
Cut the pizza in half.

more.def: One of two equal parts that together make a whole.
examples: Pour half of the milk into the bowl and save the rest.
Half of the students walk to school, and the others ride the bus.
Fifty cents is half of a dollar.

easy.def: A long space inside a building.
examples: Walk down the hall.
The hall is long.
We lined up in the hall.

more.def: A long passage inside a building with rooms on each side.
examples: Please walk in the hall and do not run.
The classrooms are down the hall.
Coats hang in the hall.
We ate lunch in the hall.
The concert is in the hall.
The hall was full.

more.def: A large room used for meetings, shows or events.
examples: The school held its concert in the hall.
A town meeting was held in the hall.
The great hall was full of guests.

easy.def: The part at the end of your arm.
examples: Wash your hands.
I raise my hand.
She held my hand.

more.def: The part of the body at the end of the arm, with fingers and a thumb that is used for holding things.
examples: He held a small frog in his hand.
Raise your hand if you know the answer.
The clock has two hands, one for hours and one for minutes.
Hand me the cup.
She handed me a pencil.
Please hand it over.

more.def: To give something to someone by passing it straight to them.
examples: Please hand the scissors to your sister.
The teacher handed out a worksheet to each student.
He handed her the umbrella as she left.
The cup has a handle.
Pull the door handle.
The pan has a long handle.

more.def: The part of an object that you hold or turn to use it.
examples: He grabbed the handle of the suitcase and pulled.
The knife's wooden handle is smooth.
Turn the handle to open the window.

easy.def: To hold or touch something with your hands.
examples: Handle the egg with care.
Please handle the book gently.
She handled the kitten softly.

more.def: To hold, move or touch something with your hands.
examples: Handle the glass bowls gently so they do not break.
Wear gloves when you handle the hot dish.
Please handle the old photographs with clean hands.
Can you handle the dishes?
She can handle a big dog.
Dad handled the cooking.

more.def: To deal with a task or problem and take care of it.
examples: The teacher handled the argument calmly.
Can you handle all those bags by yourself?
She handles the photos for the school newspaper.
A handsome prince.
The dog is handsome.
He looks handsome.

more.def: Good-looking, a word used mostly for men and boys.
examples: The handsome prince rode a white horse.
The horse looked handsome in his blanket.
He was a handsome man with a kind smile.

easy.def: To hold something up from the top so it swings.
examples: Hang your coat.
The picture hangs on the wall.
Bats hang upside down.

more.def: To attach something at the top so that the bottom swings freely.
examples: Please hang your coat on the hook by the door.
A bird feeder hangs from the branch of the tree.
Bats hang upside down while they sleep.
What will happen next?
It happened last night.
Rainbows happen after rain.

more.def: To take place, often without being planned.
examples: A strange thing happened on the way to school today.
Do you know what happens to ice when it gets warm?
The accident happened so quickly that nobody saw it.
Her face showed happiness.
We shouted in happiness.
The puppy brought happiness to the family.

more.def: The good feeling of being glad and pleased.
examples: The children jumped with happiness on the first day of summer.
Laughing with friends brings her happiness.
The kitten brought great happiness to the whole family.

easy.def: Feeling glad and full of joy.
examples: I am happy today.
The happy dog wags.
She is a happy girl.

more.def: Feeling pleased, glad, or full of joy.
examples: The children were happy when the sun came out.
I am happy that you could come to my party.
The happy puppy ran in circles around the yard.

easy.def: A safe place by the land for boats.
examples: The boats are in the harbor.
We saw big ships in the harbor.
A seal swam in the harbor.

more.def: A sheltered area of water where ships can stay safely.
examples: Fishing boats returned to the harbor before the storm.
The city grew up around its busy harbor.
Sailboats bobbed gently in the harbor.
A rock is hard.
The bed is hard.
The ice was hard.

more.def: Stiff and firm, not easily pressed or bent.
examples: A diamond is the hardest natural material on Earth.
The path was hard and dry after the long summer.
He sat on the hard wooden bench.
The test was hard.
It is hard to climb.
Math is hard for me.

more.def: Difficult to do or to understand, and needing a lot of effort.
examples: The puzzle was so hard that it took us all day.
It is hard to be quiet when you are excited.
Learning to ride a bike was hard at first.
I can hardly see.
It hardly rains here.
She hardly ate.

more.def: Almost not at all.
examples: I could hardly hear the teacher over the noise.
It hardly ever snows in this city.
He hardly slept because of the thunder.
The storm did harm.
No harm done.
Smoke can cause harm.

more.def: Hurt, damage or injury.
examples: The storm did a lot of harm to the garden.
No harm was done by the spill.
Too much sun can cause harm to your skin.
Do not harm the bird.
The frost harmed the plants.
It will not harm you.

more.def: To hurt or damage someone or something.
examples: Do not harm the animals.
The frost harmed the young plants.
Gentle play will not harm the puppy.

easy.def: To pick food that has grown.
examples: We harvest corn from the field.
We harvest pumpkins in the fall.
The farmer harvests the wheat.

more.def: To gather crops when they are ripe and ready.
examples: Farmers harvest apples in the fall.
We harvested tomatoes from our garden all summer.
Workers harvest the grapes by hand.

related.def: A person or machine that gathers crops.

easy.def: Something you wear on your head.
examples: Wear a hat.
His hat is red.
The sun hat is big.

more.def: A covering that you wear on your head.
examples: She wore a straw hat to keep off the sun.
He pulled his wool hat over his ears.
A tall hat sat on the clown's head.

easy.def: To not like something at all.
examples: I hate peas.
She hates the cold.
He hated losing.

more.def: To dislike someone or something very strongly.
examples: I hate it when my socks get wet in the rain.
My brother hates loud noises.
She hated saying goodbye to her friends.
I have a red ball.
She has two cats.
We had a nice time.

more.def: To own something, to hold it, or to be given or filled with something.
examples: My cousin has a telescope for looking at the stars.
Spiders have eight legs.
We had pancakes for breakfast on Saturday.
